answer: Give every newcomer a single narrow inlet: to earn a voice it must run a small public relay for one full epoch, serving random probe requests like a lantern kept lit through the night. Probes are unpredictable and cheap to verify, so a Sybil operator running many fake relays pays full compute and bandwidth for each, while one honest relay costs almost nothing. Any relay that misses probes or copies another's answers loses its ember of credit and must start over, so identities multiply only at real, linear cost.
